chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying:
"The butted [animal], the fallen [animal], and that which the wild beast has eaten from it, if you catch its slaughter [before it dies], then eat it."

key_terms.إِذَا أَدْرَكْتَ ذَكَاتَهُ: If you catch its slaughter (i.e., perform the ritual slaughter while it is still alive).
key_terms.النَّطِيحَةُ: An animal that dies by butting (e.g., with its horns).
key_terms.وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ: An animal that dies by falling (e.g., from a height).
key_terms.وَمَا أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ: That which the wild beast (predator) has eaten from.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from animals that die from butting, falling, or being eaten by wild beasts if they are slaughtered while still alive?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of consuming animals that die from natural causes like butting, falling, or predation, provided the owner performs the ritual slaughter (dhakat) while the animal is still alive. This ruling distinguishes these cases from *maytah* (dead meat) by emphasizing the active intervention of the owner to complete the life-sustaining process, a key principle in Shia fiqh regarding *samaki* and *dhabaih*. The hadith underscores the practical application of the Quranic prohibition of dead meat, allowing for the utilization of resources when the death was not immediate or caused by the slaughterer's direct action.
